claim: Antitrust plaintiffs satisfy the predominance requirement for class certification by using a damages model that estimates damages attributable to the antitrust injury on a class-wide basis, only if individualized determinations are not needed to allocate damages among class members.
initial_reasoning: In In Re Bystolic Antitrust Litigation, the court held that plaintiffs may satisfy the predominance requirement by employing a damages model that estimates damages attributable to the antitrust injury on a class-wide basis, provided that individualized determinations are not required to allocate damages among class members. This directly supports the claim.
